⚠️ Build error?

                
                
                

                    
🔑 If you get "keystore password was incorrect":

                    
    
                        
  • The existing keystore file may have been created with a different password
    • 
                        
  • Fix: go back to Step 2 and recreate the keystore, or enter the correct password of the existing keystore in android/key.properties
    • 
                        
  • Check storePassword and keyPassword in android/key.properties
    •

    • 
                        
  • Or close IDEs such as Android Studio or IntelliJ IDEA and try again
    • 
                    

                

                
                
                

                    
📋 Other build errors:

                    
    
                        
  • Check that the Step 2 Keystore setup is correct
    • 
                        
  • Run flutter clean and build again
    • 
                        
  • Check that android/key.properties exists and its paths are right
    • 
                        
  • Check that android/app/keystore/key.jks exists

                6
                Set up the Google Play Service Account
                
                    
                    

                        What is a Service Account?

                                An account that lets GitHub Actions call the Play Store API and upload your app automatically.
                    

                
            


            
            

                

                    
                    

                        
💡 Already have a Service Account?

                        

                            A Service Account can be reused across apps!

                        If you already made one for another Flutter app, you can use the same JSON key file.
                        

                        

                            You still need to grant it access to this app in Play Console (see the checklist below)
                        

                    

                

            


            
            

                

                    
                    

                        
🔑 Why you need a Service Account

                        

                            GitHub Actions needs it to call the Play Store API and upload the AAB automatically.
                        

                    

                

            


            
            

                
                    
                    Google Cloud Console
                
                
                    
                    Play Console
                
            


            
            

                
📋 Step-by-step: create a Service Account


                
                

                    

                        1
                        Select or create a Google Cloud project
                    

                    

                        
• Open Google Cloud Console

                        
• Click the project picker at the top

                        
• Pick an existing project or create a "New project"

                    

                


                
                

                    

                        2
                        ⚠️ Enable the Google Play Android Developer API
                        Required!
                    

                    

                        
• Type "Google Play Android Developer" in the Google Cloud Console search bar at the top

                        
• Click "Google Play Android Developer API" in the results

                        
• Click the "Enable" button (if it is already enabled, you see a "Manage" button)

                    

                    

                        💡 GitHub Actions can upload the AAB to the Play Store only after this API is enabled.
                    

                


                
                

                    

                        3
                        Create a service account
                    

                    

                        
• Left menu: "IAM & Admin" → "Service Accounts"

                        
• Click "+ Create service account" at the top

                        
• Service account name: playstore-deploy-bot

                        
• Click "Create and continue"

                    

                    

                        
📧 Service account email (you need it later to invite it in Play Console!)

                        
Email format after creation:

                        

                            playstore-deploy-bot@project-id.iam.gserviceaccount.com
                        

                        
→ Find it in the service account list or on the IAM page


                        
                        

                            
                            
                            
                            → It is shown automatically in Step 6

                        Create and download a JSON key

📍 How to register GitHub Secrets

                        
    
                            
  1. Go to your GitHub repository page
    2. 
                            
  2. Click the Settings tab
    3. 
                            
  3. In the left menu, Secrets and variables → Actions
    4. 
                            
  4. Click the New repository secret button
    5. 
                            
  5. Enter the Name and Secret value, then Add secret

📝 What each Secret is

                

                    

                        RELEASE_KEYSTORE_BASE64
                        
The Keystore file from Step 2, Base64-encoded

                    

                    

                        RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD
                        
The Store Password you entered when creating the Keystore

                    

                    

                        RELEASE_KEY_ALIAS
                        
The Key Alias you entered when creating the Keystore

                    

                    

                        RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD
                        
The Key Password you entered when creating the Keystore

                    

                    

                        GOOGLE_PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON_BASE64
                        
The Service Account JSON you uploaded in Step 6, Base64-encoded

                    

                

            


            
            

                
🔧 Optional (if you use Firebase)

                

                    

                        GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON
                        
Contents of your Firebase project's google-services.json (required if you use Firebase)

                    

                    

                        ENV_FILE
                        
Contents of your .env file (if you need environment variables)

                    It is currently set to release_status: "draft", so CI/CD only uploads to the Play Store and saves it as a "Draft".

  1. Play Console → Test and release → Latest releases and bundles
    2. 
                        
  2. Click the → on the entry whose release status is "Draft"
    3. 
                        
  3. Click [Next] at the bottom right
    4. 
                        
  4. Click [Save and publish] at the bottom right
    5. 
                        
  5. Click [Save and publish] in the dialog
    6. 
                    

                    

                        💡 After your first release is approved, change it to release_status: "completed" to deploy automatically.

🎛️ Deploy mode & release roadmap (Android)

              
The default deploy scope comes from the config file .github/config/store-deploy.json (kept in git and reviewed) or the GitHub repo Variables → ANDROID_DEPLOY_MODE. Priority is manual workflow run input > config file > repo variable > store_only. Copy store-deploy.json.example from the same folder, or add --deploy-mode store_prepare --production-rollout 0.1 to the end of the setup command above and the wizard writes the android section of this file (an existing ios section is left as is). An invalid value fails before deployment.

              
    
                
  • store_only — upload to internal testing only (default)
    • 
                
  • store_prepare — promote to a production draft (waits for "Start rollout" in the console)
    • 
                
  • store_submit — submit to production review automatically
    • 
              

              
⚠️ An app that has never been released to production cannot be promoted to production through the API. The very first release must be done by a person in Play Console; updates after that can be automated with store_submit. A build already on closed testing can be attached without rebuilding via Production → Create new release → "Add from library".

              
Production rollout percentage — GitHub repo Variables → ANDROID_PRODUCTION_ROLLOUT (above 0 and up to 1.0, default 1.0). 1.0 goes to every user as soon as review passes and cannot be undone; a lower value such as 0.1 rolls out to that share only. Raising the percentage is not automated: raise it yourself in Play Console Production → Release management, and halt the rollout on the same screen if something goes wrong.

              
"Release notes" text — by default, the CHANGELOG entry for that version. For a fixed one-line text, set STORE_WHATS_NEW_OVERRIDE in the workflow file's env. It is decided at the internal testing upload and applies to every track.

              
Notes per language — if your store has several languages, list them in metadata.template.options.store_locales in version.yml (e.g. ["ko-KR", "en-US", "ja-JP", "zh-CN"]; the first is the default language). /pro-changelog-deploy drafts the translations when it writes the release notes and asks for approval; languages without a translation get the default-language text (the store rejects empty ones). Without the key, a single text is uploaded as before.

              
If only Google Play has a different set of languages, list just that store with store_locales_play (e.g. ["ko-KR", "en-US", "ja-JP"]). Language codes Google Play does not have are skipped.
